subject: Availability backstop pricing, on-call windows & fallback credits
messages:
From: Emily Turner <emily.turner@brightpathhealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@brightpathhealth.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Inquiry: SLA options for clinical inference workload

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for taking this — BrightPath is evaluating inference providers for a clinical scoring pipeline (regulatory constraints apply). Quick context: production traffic expected to be spiky (predictable day peaks), primary region US-West, DR to US-East required. Our minimum target is 99.95% sustained availability with a clear failover/backstop policy and guaranteed escalation coverage for Sev1 issues.

We have three specific asks:
- Pricing for an SLA that includes regional failover (automated routing to DR within 15 minutes) and associated runbook support.
- Response windows: Sev1 initial acknowledge <= 15 minutes (24/7), Sev2 <= 2 hours (business hours), on-call escalation roster included.
- Failure credits: what credits do you offer per hour of outage and for failover events? Also whether credits scale with commit level.

Can you send any SKU/packages and a short sheet of pricing/credits? I attached a short security/ops requirements spreadsheet (BrightPath-Security-Needs.xlsx) to help.

Happy to schedule a 30‑minute follow-up call after we review.

Best,
Emily Turner
Director, Platform Operations
BrightPath Health

(attachment: BrightPath-Security-Needs.xlsx)
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Turner <emily.turner@brightpathhealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Inquiry: SLA options for clinical inference workload

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear brief and the attachment. Attached is a concise pricing sheet outlining three options we typically propose for regulated, production inference: Standard, Assurance, and Assurance+ (dedicated pools + prioritized routing). See attached: Redwood-SLA-pricing-v2.pdf. High level notes: 

- Standard: 99.9% SLA, business-hours on-call (M–F), credits apply for sustained outages >1 hour.
- Assurance: 99.95% SLA, 24/7 on-call, automated regional failover within our policy windows; reduced credits per hour but stronger operational guarantees.
- Assurance+: Dedicated capacity, guaranteed failover within 15 minutes, named escalation contacts, and quarterly runbook run-throughs.

Credits and uplift: credits scale by commit (12/24 month bands). We can tier credits (higher commit → larger absolute $ credits) but we also layer an on-call retainer for 24/7 prioritized response. Typical retainer ranges are $7k–$18k/month depending on coverage and response SLAs.

A few clarifying Qs to make sure pricing maps to your ask:
1) Do you need a contractual 15-minute failover SLA (we can provide an Assurance+ variant, but it requires a commit and some operational guardrails)?
2) Expected committed monthly token/embedding volume (or a monthly spend band) — that drives the marginal price and credit sizing.

If helpful, we can propose a pilot: 3-month Assurance tier with a one-month trial of an Assurance+ failover test for a small uplift. Would you be available Wed or Thu this week for a 30‑minute call?

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Senior Sales Manager — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

(attachment: Redwood-SLA-pricing-v2.pdf)
From: Emily Turner <emily.turner@brightpathhealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@brightpathhealth.com
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Inquiry: SLA options for clinical inference workload

Rachel —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the packages. Procurement flagged two items where they need flexibility for BrightPath to proceed:
1) Retainer pricing — our target for the on-call/priority retainer is $5k/month (we're looking to cap support costs while we scale).
2) Credits — we need a clearer backstop: in the event of a failover that lasts >30 minutes we expect either larger credits or a one-time remediation credit to cover our clinical re-validation run costs.

We can commit to a 12‑month spend band if discounts reach ~20–30% off the Assurance list retainer. We also prefer a pilot that includes one scheduled failover test (not live traffic) before go‑live.

Can you confirm whether you can extend a discount in that range with a 12‑month commit and specify the credit amounts for failover >30m?

Thanks — Emily

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Inquiry: SLA options for clinical inference workload (internal)

Rachel — quick guidance below. I ran numbers against the Assurance tier and a modest commit.

- Retainer: $5k/month is below our normal floor for full 24/7 prioritized rotation. We can do $5k if BrightPath accepts: (a) an increased response target for some Sev2 cases (business-hours remediation only), AND (b) a capped remediation credit (one-time failover remediation credit equal to 10% of one month’s committed spend) instead of escalating per-hour credits.

- Credits: for failover >30m we can offer either: 1) standard per-hour credit (scaled by commit), or 2) a capped remediation credit (recommended for regulated customers to simplify accounting). The capped remediation credit can be sized at 10–20% of monthly committed spend depending on commit level.

- Pilot: fully agree we should run a scheduled failover test. Make it an explicit milestone — successful test unlocks a 30‑day warranty period where we won’t charge failover penalties for test-related actions.

If we accept the $5k retainer ask, recommend we secure a 12‑month minimum commit and exclude a hard 15‑minute contractual failover SLA (we can contractually commit to an operational runbook and a 15‑minute target in Assurance+ with a higher uplift).

I’ll let Priya weigh in on legal/contract language for the remediation credit and any compliance stopgaps.

— Jonas
Head of Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Turner <emily.turner@brightpathhealth.com>
Cc: procurement@brightpathhealth.com, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Inquiry: SLA options for clinical inference workload

Emily — thanks and appreciate the clear trade-offs. Based on internal guidance we can accommodate the BrightPath asks with the following offer: 

Offer (Assurance variant, 12‑month commit):
- Retainer: $5,000/month for prioritized 24/7 on-call (covers first-response; escalation to engineering follows internal playbook).
- Failover & credits: for any unscheduled failover event >30 minutes, Redwood will provide a capped remediation credit equal to 12% of the monthly committed spend for that month. This credit replaces per-hour credits and is intended to cover clinical re-validation costs.
- Contractual SLA language: we will include operational commitments (runbooks, on-call roster, one scheduled failover test during pilot) and a target 15‑minute failover window for Assurance+ (we cannot guarantee contractual 15‑minute failover for Assurance at the $5k retainer level).
- Pilot: 60‑day pilot at Assurance pricing with one scheduled failover test (test-related actions excluded from remediation credit). Successful test finalizes go‑live terms.

Next steps: if this is acceptable, please confirm intent to proceed and procurement contact and we’ll generate a short SOW and draft amendment to the Master Services Agreement with the remediation credit language. If you want to preserve the right to a contractual 15‑minute failover SLA, we can produce an Assurance+ quote (dedicated capacity) and I’ll send that in a follow-up.

Happy to jump on a call tomorrow morning to walk through the SOW.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Senior Sales Manager — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
